Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

usually short form: я виноват / я виновата

examples.text: Она ни в чём не виновата.

examples.trans: Please, don't chase me away. I know it's my fault.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'плачивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pay extra'.

examples.trans: Will they pay us extra for covering?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет доплачивать без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to pay extra without a reason.

related.gloss: not to to pay extra (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

Written request. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'явление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'statement; application' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: + instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'over, above; at' in everyday speech.
смеяться над = to laugh at; form надо before мной

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Два года назад = two years ago. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.
Шаг назад = a step back. Core Russian adv meaning 'ago; back, backwards' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пуск'). Common masculine noun meaning 'vacation, leave' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я в отпуске-то всего два раза был.
examples.trans: I have only been on vacation twice in my whole life.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый отпуск.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new vacation.

meanings.note: A document. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sign', paired with 'подписывать'.

examples.text: Пока всё не подпишешь, не выйдешь.
examples.trans: You won't leave until you sign everything.

examples.text: Пока всё не подпишешь, отсюда не выйдешь.
examples.trans: You're not leaving here until you sign everything.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

examples.text: О чём предупреждал? Да ты что делаешь?
examples.trans: Warned me about what? Hey, what are you doing?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('drunk').

examples.text: Тогда была моя ошибка. И мы были пьяные.
examples.trans: Back then it was my mistake. And we were drunk.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

собраться.gloss: to get ready, plan to, gather

meanings.en: to intend, plan, get ready to
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get ready, plan to, gather', paired with 'собираться'.

examples.text: Ты что, уходить от меня собрался?

Are you planning to drink alcohol?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'олить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to salt', forming an aspectual pair with 'посолить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to cure') (to preserve with salt) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Соли мясо ровно через семь минут.
examples.trans: Salt the meat exactly in seven minutes.

examples.text: Соли горячее мясо ровно через семь минут после жарки.
examples.trans: Salt the hot meat exactly seven minutes into frying.

examples.text: Шеф никогда не разрешает солить блюдо, не попробовав его.
examples.trans: The chef never allows salting a dish without tasting it first.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'читаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be considered, count'.

examples.trans: Well, then it does not count.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет считаться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to be considered without a reason.

related.gloss: not to to be considered (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to act smart, play the wiseacre, philosophize pretentiously
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мничать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to act smart'.

examples.trans: No need to act smart here.

examples.text: Иди работай и не умничай здесь!
examples.trans: Go work and do not be a smart-aleck here!

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
